subject: paper:hiscock-2015
quote: Intervention compared with control families reported a greater decrease in ADHD symptoms at three and six months (adjusted mean difference for change in symptom severity -2.9, 95% confidence interval -5.5 to -0.3, P=0.03, effect size -0.3, and -3.7, -6.1 to -1.2, P=0.004, effect size -0.4, respectively).
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). RCT evidence that a behavioural sleep intervention reduced ADHD symptom severity at 3 and 6 months versus usual care.

subject: paper:hvolby-2015-sleep
quote: Current guidelines recommend assessment of sleep disturbance during evaluation of ADHD, and before initiation of pharmacotherapy, with healthy sleep practices the first-line option for addressing sleep problems.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (reused from the sleep note). Guideline framing that sleep hygiene is the first-line response to sleep problems in ADHD; medium as it states recommendation rather than an outcome.

subject: paper:van-der-heijden-2007
quote: Sleep onset advanced by 26.9 +/- 47.8 minutes with melatonin and delayed by 10.5 +/- 37.4 minutes with placebo (p < .0001).
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. RCT evidence that melatonin advances sleep onset in children with ADHD and sleep-onset insomnia.

subject: paper:van-der-heijden-2007
quote: There was no significant effect on behavior, cognition, and quality of life, and significant adverse events did not occur.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The honest limit: melatonin improved sleep timing without improving ADHD behaviour, cognition or quality of life — a sleep treatment, not an ADHD treatment.
